title: Windows IIS application pools hosting and troubleshooting
concepts: IIS routes requests through HTTP.sys, site bindings, application paths, modules and handlers. A site, application, virtual directory, and application pool are different configuration objects; confusing their boundaries causes routing, isolation, and permission errors.

An application pool is a WAS-managed process boundary with an identity, lifecycle, health, recycling, and resource behavior. ApplicationPoolIdentity provides a distinct virtual identity for ACLs; elevated built-in identities increase risk.

ASP.NET Core on IIS uses the ASP.NET Core Module (ANCM). In-process hosting runs IISHttpServer inside w3wp; out-of-process hosting runs Kestrel behind ANCM. They differ in process, request path, deployment constraints, and failure symptoms.

The .NET Hosting Bundle installs the IIS integration components needed for hosting. Framework-dependent deployments require a compatible shared runtime; self-contained deployments carry the runtime but still require the IIS module and matching architecture considerations.

Troubleshooting starts with the failure boundary: IIS logs and HTTP.sys queue, ANCM startup, application process, runtime dependency, configuration, identity ACL, or application exception. Temporary stdout logging diagnoses startup only and must be disabled after collecting evidence.

Warm-up, preload, idle timeout, recycling, overlapped rotation, startup limits, and rapid-fail protection affect availability. Changing recycling settings without understanding state, graceful shutdown, and deployment overlap can turn routine maintenance into request loss.

versionNotes.edition: ASP.NET Core 11 GA and IIS, checked 2026-11-20
items: .NET 11 became the current GA release on November 10, 2026. Current IIS and ANCM documentation is available for ASP.NET Core 11; the current troubleshooting status-code article still resolves to its ASP.NET Core 10 edition, so interpret those code mappings as the latest documented mapping and verify against the installed ANCM version. The .NET 11 IIS guide says in-process hosting is opt-in for existing apps while templates use it; inspect published web.config and app type rather than assuming project property alone determines deployed behavior.
